cards.explanation: The answer is False. “But Jonathan did not tell his father.” (1 Samuel 14:1) Jonathan, Saul's son, takes his armor-bearer and goes. Saul is Israel's king, and he's staying under the pomegranate tree in Migron.

The answer is six hundred. The troops who were with Saul numbered about six hundred men, and Saul himself was staying under the pomegranate tree in Migron. That's a small crowd for a king, friends. I've seen bigger crowds at a half-price cookie sale.

The answer is True. “But the troops did not know that Jonathan had left.” (1 Samuel 14:3) Saul has about six hundred men with him, and Ahijah the priest is among them. Jonathan was gone, and the troops were in the dark about it.

The answer is cliffs. The text says there were cliffs on both sides of the pass Jonathan intended to cross. That's not a nice flat walk to the outpost, friends. Whatever happens next, it starts with a climb.

The answer is that nothing can stop Him from saving by many or by few. That's Jonathan's whole case. He says, “Nothing can hinder the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few.” Two men against an outpost is a small number, friends. I think he's counting on who the LORD is, not on how many men he has.

The answer is that his armor-bearer says go ahead, I am with you. He says, “Do all that is in your heart. Go ahead; I am with you heart and soul.” He isn't looking for an exit. I think that's the kind of friend you want when your plan sounds bold.

The answer is that they stay right where they are. Jonathan says, “then we will stay where we are and will not go up to them.” If the Philistines say wait, the two of them wait. The plan is simple, friends. What the outpost says decides what Jonathan does.

The answer is that it will be their sign the LORD has handed the Philistines over. Jonathan says, “But if they say, ‘Come on up,’ then we will go up, because this will be our sign that the LORD has delivered them into our hands.” The invitation from the outpost is the sign. It's an odd thing to wait on, friends, but that's the plan.

The answer is that the men of the outpost call out, “Come on up, and we will teach you a lesson!” That's the sign Jonathan was waiting for. They think it's a threat, friends. Jonathan says, “Follow me… for the LORD has delivered them into the hand of Israel.”

The answer is that the Philistines fall before Jonathan. The text says, “And the Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer followed and finished them off.” (1 Samuel 14:13) Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer behind him. The men who promised a lesson are the ones who fell.

The answer is twenty. In that first assault, Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men in about half an acre of land. It's a small patch of ground for a big moment, friends. Two men started that day's story, and it's only getting bigger.
The answer is True. The text says, “Indeed, the earth quaked, and panic spread from God.” (1 Samuel 14:15) The ground shakes along with the Philistines. That's a lot of trembling in one place.

The answer is God. The text says, “…panic spread from God.” (1 Samuel 14:15) Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men, and then the whole Philistine camp shook. That part came from God, friends.

The answer is that Saul says, “Call the roll and see who has left us.” His watchmen have seen the troops melting away and scattering, so he wants a head count. The roll shows Jonathan and his armor-bearer are not there.

The answer is that the commotion keeps growing. While Saul is talking to the priest, “…the commotion in the Philistine camp continued to increase.” Things keep building over there while Saul is talking, friends. Then Saul tells the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”

The answer is Philistines in total confusion. Saul and all his troops march to the battle, “…and they found the Philistines in total confusion, with each man wielding the sword against his neighbor.” (1 Samuel 14:20) That's a heavy scene, friends. The Philistines are in confusion, and the swords are turned on their own.

The answer is False. The Hebrews who had gone up to join the Philistines “…now went over to the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.” (1 Samuel 14:21) They had been on the Philistine side, and now they switch. The Israelite side keeps growing, friends.

The answer is that they join the battle and chase the Philistines. The Israelites hiding in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were fleeing, and “…they also joined the battle in close pursuit.” (1 Samuel 14:22) They had been hiding, and now they're in the fight. That's quite a change, friends.

The answer is LORD. The text says, “So the LORD saved Israel that day…” (1 Samuel 14:23) Two men climbed a cliff, and the panic spread from God. It's the same thing Jonathan said at the start, friends, that nothing can hinder the LORD from saving. And the story isn't over yet.
